title: Rigveda 7.52: To Adityas
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 7.52: To Adityas: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 7.52 is a hymn of 3 verses addressed to Adityas. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 7, the family book of Vasiṣṭha. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 526r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 7.52.1-3 (aṣṭaka 5, adhyāya 4, varga 19); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 526r
translation.original_text:
1ā̱di̱tyāso̱ adi̍tayaḥ syāma̱ pūr de̍va̱trā va̍savo martya̱trā | sane̍ma mitrāvaruṇā̱ sana̍nto̱ bhave̍ma dyāvāpṛthivī̱ bhava̍ntaḥ ||
2mi̱tras tan no̱ varu̍ṇo māmahanta̱ śarma̍ to̱kāya̱ tana̍yāya go̱pāḥ | mā vo̍ bhujemā̱nyajā̍ta̱m eno̱ mā tat ka̍rma vasavo̱ yac caya̍dhve ||
3tu̱ra̱ṇyavo 'ṅgi̍raso nakṣanta̱ ratna̍ṁ de̱vasya̍ savi̱tur i̍yā̱nāḥ | pi̱tā ca̱ tan no̍ ma̱hān yaja̍tro̱ viśve̍ de̱vāḥ sama̍naso juṣanta ||
translation.text:
1MAY we be free from every bond, Âdityas! a castle among Gods and men, ye Vasus. Winning, may we win Varuṇa and Mitra, and, being, may we be, O Earth and Heaven.
2May Varuṇa and Mitra grant this blessing, our Guardians, shelter to our seed and offspring. Let us not suffer for another's trespass. nor do the thing that ye, O Vasus, punish.
3The ever-prompt Angirases, imploring riches from Savitar the God, obtained them. So may our Father who is great and holy, and all the Gods, accordant, grant this favour.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 526r (numbered 47r by the scribe) (OPenn image 526, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 7.51.2 ‹bhuvanasya gopāḥ pibantu somam›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 526v (numbered 47v by the scribe), begins in RV 7.53.2 ‹ṛtasya ā naḥ dyāvāpṛthivī›. Verses 7.52.1-3 end on this page.

1ādityāsaḥ | aditayaḥ | syāma | pūḥ | deva-trā | vasavaḥ | martya-trā | sanema | mitrāvaruṇā | sanantaḥ | bhavema | dyāvāpṛthivī | bhavantaḥ
2mitraḥ | tat | naḥ | varuṇaḥ | mamahanta | śarma | tokāya | tanayāya | gopāḥ | mā | vaḥ | bhujema | anya-jātam | enaḥ | mā | tat | karma | vasavaḥ | yat | cayadhve
3turaṇyavaḥ | aṅgirasaḥ | nakṣanta | ratnam | devasya | savituḥ | iyānāḥ | pi tā | ca | tat | naḥ | mahān | yajatraḥ | viśve | devāḥ | sa-manasaḥ | juṣanta
